response.overview: Starting in the 19th century, British colonial planters moved large numbers of Adivasi labourers from the Jharkhand region to clear forests and work the newly opened tea gardens of Assam and North Bengal. Generations later, their descendants, known as the "Tea Tribes," are still the backbone of the tea industry, yet remain on the margins of society. Made by Jharkhandi filmmakers Biju Toppo and Meghnath, the documentary follows the community's history of migration, exile and exploitation through testimonies and folk songs, and the filmmakers place themselves on screen as well. Billed as India's first film made in an Indigenous language, it is told mainly in Kurukh.
response.title: Kora Rajee
